question: What was India's rank in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 वां**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025** is a globally recognized tool for measuring and comparing the climate protection performance of different countries.
 
• In the **2025 ranking**, **India secured the 10th position**, reflecting its relatively strong performance in climate-related actions.
 
• The CCPI evaluates countries based on four categories: **Greenhouse Gas Emissions (40%)**, **Renewable Energy (20%)**, **Energy Use (20%)**, and **Climate Policy (20%)**.
 
• India’s improved ranking was primarily due to its **ambitious renewable energy targets** and commitment to achieving **net-zero emissions by 2070**.
 
• Despite its high ranking, India still faces challenges in reducing overall emissions and transitioning from coal-based energy sources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **What is CCPI?**

 
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)** is an annual publication by **Germanwatch**, the **NewClimate Institute**, and the **Climate Action Network (CAN)**.
 
• It assesses and ranks 60 countries and the European Union, which together are responsible for over **90% of global greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The index promotes transparency in international climate politics and highlights countries that are taking effective climate action.
 
 
 
• **India’s Climate Actions:**
 
 
• India has committed to achieving **50% of its electricity generation capacity** from **renewable energy sources** by 2030.
 
• It has also launched initiatives like the **National Solar Mission** and the **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan** to reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• India’s **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** is a key initiative aimed at global cooperation in solar energy development.
 
 
 
• **Categories in CCPI:**
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions:** Measures a country’s progress in reducing overall emissions.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** Evaluates the share of renewable energy in the energy mix and its growth rate.
 
• **Energy Use:** Assesses energy efficiency and overall consumption levels.
 
• **Climate Policy:** Analyzes a country’s national and international climate policies and their effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Denmark**, **Sweden**, and **Norway** frequently top the CCPI rankings due to their strong climate policies and renewable energy adoption.
 
• In contrast, countries heavily reliant on coal and fossil fuels, such as **Australia** and **Saudi Arabia**, often rank lower.
 
• The CCPI encourages nations to adopt best practices from high-performing countries and address shortcomings in their climate strategies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Initiatives:**

 
 
• India has set a target of achieving **500 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2030.
 
• It is also one of the few countries on track to meet its commitments under the **Paris Agreement**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for India:**
 
 
• India’s coal dependency remains a significant hurdle in achieving sustainable energy transition.
 
• Rapid urbanization and population growth pose challenges in reducing overall emissions.
 
 
 
• **International Cooperation:**
 
 
• India plays a key role in global climate negotiations and has emphasized the principle of **“Common but Differentiated Responsibilities”** in international forums.
 
• It has also partnered with countries like **France** to promote solar energy through the **International Solar Alliance**.
